sections.presenting_complaint: Review of low mood, 4 weeks after starting sertraline.
sections.history: Low mood for about 3 months. Slight improvement in mornings only; mood 2–3/10. Early morning waking at 4 am. Reduced appetite with approximately half a stone weight loss. Denies passive suicidal ideation (would be easier not to wake up) most days for the last two weeks. No active suicidal thoughts, plans or preparations. No previous self-harm or suicide attempts. Protective factors: nephew and mother. Alcohol: initially said four pints a week; on sister's challenge, confirmed four cans most nights, more at weekends. No drug use. Mild nausea in first week of sertraline, now resolved; no agitation. Attended with sister, with consent.
sections.medications_allergies: Sertraline 50 mg once daily (4 weeks). No known drug allergies.
sections.examination: Appears tired, reduced eye contact, slowed speech. Speech coherent. No psychotic features. PHQ-9: 19.
sections.impression: Moderately severe depression with partial response to sertraline. Passive suicidal ideation without plan or intent; protective factors present. Harmful alcohol use.
sections.plan: Increase sertraline to 200 mg once daily. Refer to NHS Talking Therapies and self-referral details given. Inform the community crisis team. Review in 1 week. Agreed to hand stockpiled medicines to sister. Alcohol support service details given; aim to reduce gradually.
sections.safety_netting: Crisis plan agreed: if thoughts worsen or he considers acting on them, call NHS 111 (mental health option) or Samaritans 116 123; if unable to keep himself safe, call 999 or attend A&E. Sister has the numbers.
